description: Increased risk of bleeding. Both drugs affect hemostasis through different mechanisms.
recommendation: Avoid combination unless benefits outweigh risks. Monitor INR closely.

description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, increasing warfarin levels and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Monitor INR within 3-5 days of starting ciprofloxacin. Dose adjustment may be needed.

description: Metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism, increasing anticoagulant effect.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 25-50%. Monitor INR every 2-3 days.

description: Omeprazole may increase warfarin levels via CYP2C19 inhibition.
recommendation: Monitor INR when starting or stopping omeprazole.

description: Risk of lactic acidosis. Iodinated contrast can cause acute kidney injury, reducing metformin clearance.
recommendation: Hold metformin 48 hours before and after contrast administration. Check renal function.

description: ACE inhibitors reduce aldosterone, causing potassium retention. Combined with K+ supplements, hyperkalemia risk.
recommendation: Monitor serum potassium regularly. Avoid routine K+ supplementation.

description: Both cause potassium retention. Combined use significantly increases hyperkalemia risk.
recommendation: If used together, start spironolactone at lowest dose. Monitor K+ within 1 week.

description: Amiodarone increases digoxin levels by 70-100% by reducing renal and non-renal clearance.
recommendation: Reduce digoxin dose by 50% when starting amiodarone. Monitor digoxin levels.

description: Clarithromycin is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor, drastically increasing statin levels and rhabdomyolysis risk.
recommendation: Contraindicated. Use azithromycin as alternative antibiotic.

description: Amlodipine moderately inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin exposure.
recommendation: Do not exceed simvastatin 20mg daily with amlodipine.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal clearance of methotrexate, increasing toxicity risk (pancytopenia, nephrotoxicity).
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs with high-dose methotrexate. With low-dose, monitor CBC and renal function.

description: Both are folate antagonists. Combined use increases risk of bone marrow suppression.
recommendation: Avoid combination. If necessary, supplement with folinic acid and monitor CBC.

description: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandins, decreasing lithium clearance by 20-25%.
recommendation: Monitor lithium levels when starting/stopping NSAIDs. Use sulindac as safer alternative.

description: ACE inhibitors reduce lithium clearance, potentially causing toxicity.
recommendation: Reduce lithium dose. Monitor levels within 5 days of starting ACE inhibitor.

description: Risk of serotonin syndrome — potentially fatal. Excessive serotonergic activity.
recommendation: Absolutely contraindicated. Wait 14 days (5 weeks for fluoxetine) between switching.

description: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing conversion of clopidogrel to active metabolite.
recommendation: Use pantoprazole instead of omeprazole. Separate doses by 12 hours if unavoidable.

description: Aluminum/magnesium antacids chelate ciprofloxacin, reducing absorption by 90%.
recommendation: Take ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

description: Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2, increasing theophylline levels and toxicity risk.
recommendation: Reduce theophylline dose by 30-50%. Monitor theophylline levels.

description: Calcium chelates tetracyclines, significantly reducing oral absorption.
recommendation: Separate administration by at least 2 hours.

description: Iron chelates tetracyclines, reducing absorption of both drugs.
recommendation: Separate by at least 2-3 hours.

description: Amlodipine may increase cyclosporine levels. Both metabolized by CYP3A4.
recommendation: Monitor cyclosporine levels when adding or adjusting amlodipine dose.

description: Additive negative inotropic and chronotropic effects. Risk of severe bradycardia, heart block, and heart failure.
recommendation: Avoid combination, especially IV verapamil with any beta blocker.

description: Amiodarone inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin levels and rhabdomyolysis risk.
recommendation: Do not exceed simvastatin 20mg/day with amiodarone.

description: Rifampicin is a potent CYP3A4 inducer, reducing contraceptive efficacy.
recommendation: Use alternative contraception during and 28 days after rifampicin treatment.

description: Rifampicin induces CYP enzymes, dramatically reducing warfarin levels.
recommendation: May need 2-3x warfarin dose increase. Monitor INR closely when starting/stopping.

description: Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9, increasing warfarin levels and bleeding risk.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 25%. Monitor INR within 3-5 days.

description: Erythromycin inhibits CYP3A4, increasing carbamazepine levels and toxicity.
recommendation: Monitor carbamazepine levels. Consider azithromycin as alternative.

description: Grapefruit inhibits intestinal CYP3A4, increasing statin absorption and levels.
recommendation: Avoid grapefruit with simvastatin/atorvastatin. Rosuvastatin/pravastatin are safer.

description: Severe additive vasodilation causing potentially fatal hypotension.
recommendation: Absolutely contraindicated. Do not use within 24 hours (48h for tadalafil).

description: Both cause potassium retention, significantly increasing hyperkalemia risk.
recommendation: If combined, monitor serum potassium within 1 week and regularly thereafter.

description: Both increase serotonin. Risk of serotonin syndrome (tremor, hyperthermia, agitation).
recommendation: Use with caution at lowest doses. Educate patient on serotonin syndrome symptoms.

description: SSRIs impair platelet aggregation. Combined with NSAIDs, increased GI bleeding risk.
recommendation: Consider adding a PPI for gastroprotection if combination is necessary.

description: Carbamazepine induces CYP3A4, reducing contraceptive hormone levels.
recommendation: Use non-hormonal or high-dose contraception. Consider IUD.

description: Complex interaction: valproate displaces phenytoin from protein binding and inhibits metabolism.
recommendation: Monitor free phenytoin levels (not total). Adjust doses based on clinical response.

description: Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, blocking azathioprine metabolism. Risk of severe myelosuppression.
recommendation: Reduce azathioprine dose by 67-75%. Monitor CBC weekly for first month.

description: Increased risk of tendon rupture, especially in elderly patients.
recommendation: Use combination with caution in patients >60 years. Monitor for tendon pain.

description: Additive dopamine blockade. Increased risk of extrapyramidal symptoms and tardive dyskinesia.
recommendation: Avoid combination if possible. Use domperidone as alternative prokinetic.

description: Additive CNS and respiratory depression. Risk of fatal overdose.
recommendation: Avoid combination when possible. If necessary, use lowest effective doses of both.

description: Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9, increasing warfarin effect. Risk persists months after stopping.
recommendation: Reduce warfarin dose by 30-50%. Monitor INR weekly for first 6-8 weeks.

description: Spironolactone reduces renal clearance of digoxin and interferes with digoxin assay.
recommendation: Monitor digoxin levels using chemiluminescent assay. May need dose reduction.

description: Beta blockers mask tachycardia symptoms of hypoglycemia and may prolong hypoglycemic episodes.
recommendation: Use cardioselective beta blockers (bisoprolol). Educate patient on non-adrenergic hypoglycemia signs.

description: Carbamazepine induces theophylline metabolism, reducing its efficacy.
recommendation: Monitor theophylline levels. May need dose increase.

description: Calcium reduces levothyroxine absorption by forming insoluble complexes.
recommendation: Separate administration by at least 4 hours.

description: Iron reduces levothyroxine absorption.
recommendation: Separate by at least 4 hours. Take levothyroxine on empty stomach.

description: Alcohol increases risk of metformin-associated lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Avoid excessive alcohol consumption. Educate patient on lactic acidosis symptoms.

description: Clarithromycin inhibits CYP3A4, markedly increasing tacrolimus levels and nephrotoxicity risk.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Use azithromycin as alternative.

description: NSAIDs further reduce renal blood flow in cyclosporine-treated patients. Risk of nephrotoxicity.
recommendation: Avoid combination. Monitor renal function if unavoidable.

description: Abrupt clonidine withdrawal with beta blocker can cause rebound hypertensive crisis.
recommendation: Taper clonidine before stopping. Do not stop both simultaneously.

description: Antacids chelate doxycycline, reducing absorption.
recommendation: Separate by 2-3 hours.

description: Trimethoprim blocks renal potassium excretion. With ACE inhibitors, hyperkalemia risk increases.
recommendation: Monitor potassium within 2 days of starting trimethoprim in patients on ACE inhibitors.
